chapters.html:
The morning light was thin as it filtered through the kitchen window. Mydei stood by the sink, fingers wrapped around a lukewarm mug of tea he hadn’t touched. The taste had been off lately. 

Everything had either been too strong or too bland. He’d chalked up to stress, maybe from not sleeping enough, or missing Phainon more than he wanted to admit. 

It had been a couple of weeks since Phainon left for his term abroad, and even though they texted constantly and video called in the quiet hours of the night, there was an ache in Mydei’s chest that hadn’t really gone away. 

His stomach churned again. 

He set the mug down, breathing through the discomfort. It wasn’t the first time this happened. Mornings were… unreliable. He used to wake up, sort through paperwork for the new bakery, head to class while humming along to his favourite playlist. But now, he was light-headed, a little queasy, and sensitive to smells. 

Mydei let out a small sigh. 

“Just tired. That’s all,” he mumbled to himself before reaching for his phone. There were a few messages from Phainon. He sent photos of old books, a voice memo describing a cathedral he’d seen, a sleepy “wish you were here” from around 3am. 

Mydei listened to that last one twice. Then a third time. 

☼

The library was hushed save for the scratch of pens and the occasional clatter of keyboards. Mydei sat at a table with Castorice and Cipher, textbooks and notes littered across the table. 

He’d been trying to focus on the text in front of him, but the words kept swimming. His head felt cloudy and his stomach wasn’t settling. The drink Castorice had brought him earlier still sat untouched. 

“—dei?” Castorice’s voice cut through his thoughts. 

Mydei blinked. “Hm?”

“I asked if you wanted to grab lunch soon?”

“Yeah…” he muttered as Cipher tapped the back of his head with a pen. 

“Agh, you’re zoning out again,” she groaned. “What’s up with you? You’ve been weird all afternoon.”

“I’m fine,” Mydei said, though it sounded unconvincing. He forced a smile as he scribbled something useless in the margin of his notes. “Just been feeling a little…off.”

Castorice closed her book, folding her hands neatly on the table. “How so?”

Mydei let out a small sigh. “I don’t know…I’ve been queasy in the morning, not as hungry—It’s probably just some bug,” he brushed off. 

Cipher leaned back in her chair, a smirk forming across her lips. “You know what that sounds like to me?” she asked, pausing, most likely for dramatic effect, “sounds like our little prince is pregnant~”

Castorice elbowed Cipher, muttering something about not joking about something like that as heat rose to her cheeks. But Mydei just laughed. 

It was ridiculous. 

It really was. 

Mydei? Pregnant? 

Pregnant. 

Pregnant…?

The words stuck with something inside him. He laughed again nervously, trying to push away the sudden flutter of unease in his stomach. 

“De?” Castorice asked softly. 

He glanced up. “What?”

“What is it?”

“Nothing,” he insisted, a little too fast. His heart picked up speed, fingers drumming against his notebook. “It’s just—It’s absurd, that’s all. Phainon and I were careful. We’re always careful,” he muttered. “It’s not like I could actually be…”

His voice trailed off. 

Phainon’s skin and the press of his mouth against his throat. The night before he left. The way he’d murmured something about not wanting to stop, and Mydei hadn’t pressed the issue either. His stomach churned. 

“God, you two are so serious,” Cipher drawled out. “I was only joking.”

He swallowed hard and nodded, forcing a smile that didn’t quite reach his eyes. “I know,” he said, unsure. 

Did he?

☼

Mydei didn’t make eye contact with the cashier when he paid for the tests, tucking them into his bag like they were something scandalous. His heart was pounding. He kept telling himself it was just to rule it out. It was just a precaution—and after it was over, he could sleep easy again. 

Back home, he set the boxes on the bathroom counter and stared at them. 

He reached for one, but hesitated. He splashed his face with some water just to delay opening it before he looked at himself in the mirror and took in a breath. 

When he finally did it. The tests sat flipped on the counter. He’d been drumming his fingers against the counter, closing his eyes as he let his phone timer tick down. 

It’s nothing. I’m just tired. It’s nothing. 

A beep. He cracked once eye open, then flipped over the first test. 

Two lines. 

He blinked before flipping over the second one. 

Two lines. 

He picked up the third one, sitting on the edge of the tub, hands trembling as he turned over the little stick as if the result would be any different. 

Pregnant. 

He let out a sound. Then, as the quiet settled in around him, his other hand moved to rest against his stomach. 

“Phainon,” he whispered, eyes stinging. 

How was he supposed to tell him something like this?

☼ 

The bedroom was quiet save for the rustle of leaves outside. Mydei stared at the ceiling above, listening to the static on his phone just before Phainon’s voice came through. 

“You’re still up?” Phainon asked through the phone, his tone was warm, but exhausted around the edges. “It’s late, isn’t it?”

“You said you’d be done around this time,” Mydei murmured, shifting the blanket as his hand instinctively rested on his stomach. “I didn’t want to miss you.”

There was a pause on the other end, and then the sound of Phainon’s laugh, soft and pleased. “You texted me ‘call when you can’ like it was something important, but you just wanted to hear my voice, huh?”

Mydei hesitated for a second, humming as he closed his eyes. “Is that a problem?”

“Mm not a problem,” Phainon teased, voice dipping. “But it does make me suspicious. The Mydeimos getting sentimental without reason?”

“I’m not sentimental,” Mydei countered, playfully rolling his eyes. 

“Mhm,” Phainon chuckled again. “You just wanted to listen to me breathe. You could’ve told me you were desperate.”

Mydei rolled onto his back, sighing—embarassed by how close that was to the truth. “You’re insufferable.”

“Maybe,” he said easily. “But admit it—you missed me so much you couldn’t go another minute without my voice. 

Mydei closed his eyes. The words he should’ve been saying just wouldn’t come out. There’s something I need to tell you. I’m… pregnant. The weight pressed down on his throat, but instead, he swallowed and whispered. “Maybe I did.”

There was a quiet sigh on the other end, tender, aching. “I wish I was there.”

“Me too,” Mydei said, fingers curling tighter in the blanket. He was just about to speak when Phianon cursed softly. 

“Ah—shit, babe. I gotta go. I’ll call you soon?”

“Yeah,” Mydei kept his voice steady even as the thought pressed at the back of his mind: I should’ve told him. 

☼ 

The knock came just after noon. 

When Mydei opened the door, Castroice stood there in a pale lilac sweater, her scarf tucked in loosely and her hands folded in front of her. 

“...Hi,” she said gently. “Can I come in?”

He stepped aside without a word to let her as she dropped her bag by the door and toed off her shoes. 

“You haven’t been to the library,” she pointed out, turning toward him. “I was…starting to worry.”

“It’s been a long week,” Mydei muttered, rubbing the back of his neck. 

Castorice gave a faint nod and sat down on the couch. “Did something happen between you and Phainon? Cipher is convinced you’re fighting.”

Mydei blinked, then let out a weak laugh as he sat across from her. “We’re not fighting.”

“Was it what Cipher said the other day? You know she was only joking, but if it offended you in some way, I can—”

“It’s not that,” Mydei cut in. “Not exactly but—” he paused, looking down at the floor, arms crossed loosely over his chest. 

This would be the first time he’d say it out loud and that made it feel a lot more real. 

Castorice waited a moment longer before she spoke. “Do you want to talk about it?”

Mydei averted his gaze, hand resting on his stomach—hoping it was enough for Castorice to understand. When he turned back to look at her, her eyes were wide. 

“De, are you…?”

“I’m pregnant,” he nodded. 

She nodded solemnly before reaching over to place a hand atop of his. “Have you told Phai?”

Mydei shook his head. “Not yet. I haven’t... I haven't found the right time," he admitted. "He’s pursuing what he loves, and I don’t want to take that away from him by dropping something like this on him. He shouldn't have to focus on me.”

Cas’ eyes softened. “You don’t have to figure it all out right now, but I don’t think there is a right time for something like this.”

“He's miles away. He left and I had to get used to him not being here and now—” his voice cracked. “Everything’s changing... what if he's upset?”

She leaned in to rest her head lightly against his shoulder. “I have faith in the person I know Phainon to be,” she pulled back slightly to poke a finger to his chest. “He loves you. We both know he’s not going to be upset and I know you’ll both make the decision that’s best for you. But no matter what happens, Cipher and I are here for you. We love you too, you know."

For the first time in days, Mydei let himself lean into her warmth, feeling a little more at ease. 

☼

The call connected after a couple of rings, Mydei’s laptop screen flickered before Phainon’s face showed up. His hair was mused and he looked tired but he still smiled the moment he saw Mydei. 

“This is soooo unfair,” Phainon groaned. “You’re wearing my hoodie and I’m not even there to take it off of you.”

A smile tugged at Mydei’s lips even through the tightness in his chest. “You’ll survive.”

“It’s torture, that’s what it is,” he sighed, flopping back dramatically onto his bed, phone still in hand. “What’s on your mind? Your text sounded urgent?”

Mydei hesitated. His fingers twisted into the hem of the hoodies, the fabric didn’t really smell like Phainon anymore after all these weeks. He’d told himself all day he was going to do it. That he couldn’t hide it any longer. This was something Phainon deserved to know. 

“I…” He swallowed. “I just wanted to see your face. Hear your voice.”

Phainon tilted his head. “Sentimental again, huh? Maybe I should go away more often.”

“I’m serious,” Mydei murmured. His voice was quieter than he meant it to be. “I miss you.”

Something in Phainon’s expression shifted, all the teasing slipping away. He let out a small huff, eyes softening. “I miss you too. More than you could ever imagine.”

The silence stretched between them, Mydei could feel his heart in his throat. He couldn’t let another opportunity slip away. Finally, he let out a breath. 

“Phai…” His hand moved unconsciously to his stomach. “I need to tell you something.”

Phainon straightened, sitting up now with his back against the headboard. "Did something happen?”

Mydei’s eyes burned. He forced himself not to look away, not to let his resolve waver. “I’m…I’m pregnant.”

For a moment, Phainon didn’t move at all. Just stared, lips parted like he hadn’t fully comprehended. 

“You’re—” he voice caught. “You’re pregnant… Mydei, you’re actually pregnant?” 

Mydei gave a nod, fingers tightening in the fabric at his waist. “Eight—No nine weeks now. I know I should’ve told you sooner. I just wasn’t sure how or if you’d be…upset.”

“Upset?” Phainon’s voice cracked, eyes wide as he laughed in disbelief. “Mydei,” he ran a hand through his hair, clearly overwhelmed, “you’re having our baby. How could I ever be upset? I could never—God, I should be there. I can't believe you've been going through this alone."

Tears stung at Mydei’s eyes, but he smiled despite it. “So… you’re okay with it?”

Phainon pressed his fingers to the screen like he could reach through it. “Are you? No matter what you say, I’m with you every step of the way.”

Mydei closed his eyes for a moment, a few tears slipping down his cheeks before he nodded. “I am.”

Phainon smiled at the other end, his eyes lighting up. He pushed a hand through his hair, breathless. “We’re really having a baby,” he whispered, letting out a shaky laugh as his voice broke on the last word. 

“Yeah, we’re having a baby,” Mydei echoed as comfortable silence washed over them. 

“I should come back," Phainon broke the silence.

“Phai—”

“No, listen,” he said, already propping his phone up against something and grabbing his laptop. “I could probably find a flight and be there by morning. You’re more important to me than anything.”

Mydei sat forward, pulling his laptop into his lap. “Phainon.”

“I mean it. You’re pregnant, babe. What am I even doing if I’m not there for you?”

“I know,” Mydei said, a little more forcefully than he meant to. That got Phainon to pause. “You’ve worked so hard for this. It’s only a couple of months and you’ll be back. I don’t want you to drop everything right now… just trust me, okay?”

The ache in Phainon’s expression softened. “Are you really okay?”

“I am,” Mydei said. “You’ll come home when you’re supposed to. We’ll figure out everything then. But I’ve got this. Besides—I’ll see you during breaks, won’t I?”

Phainon exhaled, pushing out his bottom lip. “I hate being away from you,” he pouted before narrowing his eyes. “You have to text me everyday and call me everytime you’re in for an appointment,” he said. “And you have to take pictures everyday.”

“Every few weeks is the best you’re going to get.”

“I don’t want to miss anything.”

“Phainon,” Mydei said dryly. “Nothing is going to change in a single day.”

He let out a soft ‘hmph,’ before placing a hand on his chest. “Suit yourself, you can deprive your very loving boyfriend of bump pictures.”

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes as Phainon continued his musings. Warmth pooled in his stomach at the idea of it all. He smiled faintly at the thought of them being parents.

“Hey Phai?”

“Hm?”

“I love you.”

Mydei had been exhausted lately between the pregnancy, the bouts of nausea, sorting through the seemingly endless paperwork for the bakery, and his class. He was in the library with Cas and Cipher, head resting against the table even though he knew he should’ve been getting work done. 

His phone buzzed once against the table. Then again. Then again. 

And again. 

“Are you going to get that?” Cipher asked, not looking up from her laptop. 

Mydei huffed, not bothering to hide the annoyance and slight affection in his voice. “It’s Phainon.”

Castorice glanced up from her book, worry crossing her features. “Did something happen?”

“No,” Mydei lifted his phone slightly, grabbing his phone and unlocking it with his thumb. “He’s just like this now.”

Cipher glanced over, snorting. “Heh~ that’s what you get for letting him knock you up,” she said a little too loudly. A few heads turned in their direction and Castorice flushed, elbowing her and mumbling something about keeping her voice down. 

Mydei just rolled his eyes before turning to the screen. It was flooded with messages

Phainon 

hello gorgeous <3

did you drink water today?

have you eaten yet?? be honest

don’t overwork yourself

mydei

mydeiiiiii

mydeimos

Mydei sighed before typing out a reply:

I can’t believe I let YOU get me pregnant

stop texting me, I’m working

Mydei stuffed his phone in his pocket, so they could pack up their things. They migrated to the cafe nearby. Mydei had caved to his hunger and was quietly nibbling at a sandwich while Castorice continued typing her notes and Cipher was stirring three sugar packets into a single shot of espresso. 

Mydei’s phone buzzed again. 

Cipher’s eyes flicked to it. “Is that your baby daddy again?” she drawled out the last word. 

Mydei narrowed his eyes on her. “He’s my boyfriend,” he corrected while Cas laughed softly. He looked over at her. “Not you too.”

She shrugged. “It was funny,” she said sheepishly as Cipher threw an arm around her. 

A moment passed before Cipher leaned forward to grab Mydei’s phone clear off the table, not even giving him the opportunity to react. 

“Hey!” Mydei reached for it, but she already turned in her chair, shielding the screen with her back. 

“Oh-ho-ho, what do we have here~” she dragged out the words, voice dipping low. “Oh my, little prince.”

Mydei’s eyes widened instantly. “What? What—give it back.”

“I knew there was something going on behind all those ‘drink water’ texts.”

“Cipher!” Mydei half stood, heat rising to his cheeks as he reached across the table to grab his the phone. “What did he send?!”

She let out a scandalized gasp. “Oh my. He really—”

Mydei snatched the phone out of her hands. 

He stared. 

The latest message from Phainon was there. 

Phainon

I miss you even if you get a little mean

Mydei blinked. 

“...it’s nothing.”

Cipher collapsed back in her chair, laughing as she wiped a stray tear from her eye. “You should’ve seen the look on your face. Did you really think—what? He sent a nude?”

Mydeu averted his gaze. “It’s not impossible,” he muttered

The late afternoon light filtered in through the sheer curtains. Mydei stood in front of the full length mirror in his bedroom, shirt tugged up just enough to reveal the subtle curve of his belly. It wasn’t much, just a slight swell, but it was noticeable, especially to him. 

He titled his head, adjusting the angle. His fingers rested just beneath the bump. It still felt strange, surreal. Like something he was watching happen except it really was him. 

“Alright,” he mumbled under his breath, “Let’s get this over with for papa, little one.” 

He picked up his phone and snapped the photo quickly. He looked at it once. Then twice. His hair was a little messy and he was smiling. He didn’t hate it. 

He pulled up Phainon’s contact, typing out a message: 

thought you might want an update 

He attached the photo and hit send. 

Almost immediately, the typing dots appeared. 

Phainon 

I just stopped breathing

You’re so beautiful 

Mydei rolled his eyes playfully. 

We miss you 

Phainon 

I miss you more 

☼

The knock on the apartment door was quick and impatient enough that it could only belong to one person. 

Mydei was already on his feet, heart thudding faster than it should’ve. He hadn’t expected Phain to be early, but then again, of course he was. 

He opened the door and barely had time to register the sight of him before Phainon surged forward and wrapped him up in his arms. 

"Mydei you—!” Phainon practically lifted him off the ground, arms locked around his waist, spinning them once in the doorway before Mydei could think about protesting. “You look incredible. I missed you. I missed you so much.”

“Phainon!” Mydei laughed, breath catching as his feet hovered for a second. “Put me dow—mmph”

He was cut off by Phainon’s lips pressing to his with an exaggerated “mwah” sound. Followed by another. Then another. 

“Let—” kiss

“Me—” kiss

“Have—” kiss

“This—”  kiss

“Phainon,” Mydei gasped between the onslaught of affection, cheeks burning. “I will, but can we please go inside?”

Phainon finally paused, lips hovering dangerously close to his jaw. “...Right. Yes. Inside. Good plan. But just so you know—you opened the door looking like that. I could’ve dropped to my knees on the spot.”

Mydei huffed, turning and walking back into the apartment, trying not to smile too much as Phainon followed after him with a grin. 

He dropped his bags by the door, kicking the door shut with his foot. 

“Now…” he stepped closer, voice dipping low as his hands found Mydei’s waist. “Where were we?” 

Mydei bit back a smile, playfully rolling his eyes. He brought one hand to rest against Phainon’s chest before leaning in to kiss him this time. 

☼ 

The living room was dimly lit by the soft light of the evening sun slipping past the curtain. They sat at the table across from each other, eating between bouts of laughter, their knees brushing occasionally. 

Mydei had wanted to cook, but he’d been on his feet all day long, so Phainon had insisted that they order something instead. 

Mydei plucked a fry from Phainon’s plate, biting into as he eyed the two suitcases that still sat untouched by the door even after they’d unpacked two others. 

“You know,” he said, tilting his head, “for someone supposedly visiting for just a week, you packed like you’re staying forever.”

Phainon didn’t look up right away, but then he cleared his throat. “Ah…I was going to wait until later to say this,” he said, wiping his hands on a napkin. “But…I’m not going back.”

Mydei blinked, hands pausing in place. “What?”

Phainon held up a hand, “Before you say anything, I’m not abandoning the program. I talked to the department weeks ago and they’re letting me continue at the university here. I might have to travel back sometimes, but I’m staying here. With you.”

“You…really did that?” Mydei huffed. “I’m only five months—there’s still time.”

“Exactly,” Phainon said gently. “I don’t wanna keep missing things. I want to be here. For the appointments. The mood swings. Every kick. To massage your back at 3 am. All of it.”

Mydei reached over to lace their fingers together as tears threatened to fall. God, he loved him so much. 

Phainon shifted his chair closer, opening his arms for Mydei to lean into, kissing the top of his head. 

“I might take you up on that massage,” Mydei mumbled. 

☼ 

The bedroom was quiet, the light from the light spilling inside. The sheets were tangled at their legs, half-forgotten. Phainon’s hands rested gently on Mydei’s waist, thumb brushing along the hem of his shirt—one he’d stolen from Phainon a few days ago. 

They hadn’t had much time since he’d gotten back. Between unpacking, meeting old friends, and back-to-back doctor’s appointments, things had gone busy to say the least. 

But now, finally, they weren’t exactly in a rush. 

Phainon leaned in, lips brushing against Mydei’s slowly, lingering just long enough fro his breath to catch. Mydei kissed him back with urgency, deeper this time, fingers digging into Phainon’s bare shoulder as their mouths pressed together again and again. 

Mydei tilted his head back when Phainon kissed just below his ear, letting out a quiet, unguarded sound. Phainon responded with a low groan of his own, his hand sliding further up beneath Mydei’s shirt. 

“You sure?” he murmured, voice rough with restraint. His thumb stroked over the swell of Mydei’s belly, careful but enough to be possessive. “We can stop.” 

“I’m pregnant, not made of glass,” Mydei said, threading his fingers into Phainon’s hair and pulling him back down into a kiss that was all tongue and teeth and frustration. “If you stop,” he said against his mouth. “I swear I’ll make you sleep on the couch.”

Phainon grinned, eyes dark, and kissed him harder. 

Their clothes were peeled off, Phainon’s shirt tossed somewhere toward the end of the bed, Mydei’s pants half-kicked off before Phainon helped him the rest of the way. 

Every touch was reverent like his hands were mapping familiar skin that he needed to relearn all over again. 

“Mine,” Phainon mouthed down Mydei’s chest, his voice low. “Is this okay?”

“Phai please,” Mydei breathed out. “Shut—up and touch me.”

He didn’t hesitate. His hand slid lower, drawing a sharp inhale from Mydei. “You’re perfect,” he mumbled, trailing kisses down his chest and stomach. “So perfect.”

Mydei gasped when Phainon finally moved lower again. His hands raked down his back, nails dragging lightly as Phainon finally gave him what he needed. 

☼

The front door clicked open and shut softly behind Phainon. 

“I come bearing gifts,” he called out as he kicked off his shoes. “I made friends with the girl at the bakery. She said I'd make a good dad.”

Mydei glanced up at him from where he was preparing dinner in the kitchen. “You will."

Phainon just grinned, setting the box down on the counter and lifting the lid to reveal six delicately frosted cupcakes. “Ready?” 

“You’re the one vibrating.”

Phainon pouted. “I am not,” he said without much conviction as he reached for one of the cupcakes and passed another to Mydei. “Together?”

Mydei nodded. 

They both closed their eyes as they bit into the soft cake. The unmistakable taste of raspberry hit Mydei’s tongue as Phainon made a noise somewhere between a gasp and a laugh. 

Mydei opened his eyes, pulling back to see the evidence. The filling inside the cupcake was unmistakably pink and studded with raspberries. “A girl…”

Phainon dropped his half eaten cupcake onto the counter and reached for him immediately, wrapping Mydei in his arms. 

“A girl,” he said into Mydei’s neck. “We’re going to have a daughter.”

Mydei was still stunned, arms loosely around Phainon’s shoulder. “I wasn’t supposed to cry,” he muttered, voice thick, and mentally chalking it up to the hormones. 

Phainon pulled back just enough to look at him, wiping his eyes with the pads of his thumbs before his hands slipped down to his stomach. “She’s going to be gorgeous,” he whispered. “Just like her mama.”

Mydei shook his head. “Flatterer.”

Phainon just made a satisfied sound as he leaned in to kiss him. 

☼ 

The sound of wood pieces clinking together and the occasional curse under Phainon’s breath filled the living room. He was sitting cross-legged on the rug, sleeves pushed up to his elbows, brow furrowed as he studied the instruction manual.

He’d been muttering things like ‘not that isn’t it’ and ‘wait that’s not right’ after telling Mydei that he wasn’t allowed to lift a finger. 

Mydei had taken to the couch behind him, wrapped in a thin blanket, his cheek resting against a throw pillow. He was halfway asleep, drowsy from lunch and the weight of the day. He shifted shifted slightly, placing a hand on his stomach to adjust. 

Then he felt a flutter. 

He blinked away the haze of sleep. Another kick followed, this one firmer. 

“Hm someone’s active,” he mumbled. 

Phainon froze mid-screw, glancing over his shoulder. “Huh?”

“She’s kicking,” Mydei said, reaching for him. Phainon scrambled over, forgetting the crib-in-progress entirely as Mydei took his hand and guided it to the spot. “Here.”

Kick. 

He let out a breathless laugh, eyes wide. “She’s strong—she totally gets that from me.”

“Mm no,” Mydei countered. “She gets that from me.”

Phainon narrowed his eyes. “Prove it then.” 

Mydei shook his head. “No, Phainon, I’m not fighting you when I’m pregnant with your baby. It’s reckless and I can’t believe you’d even suggest—”

“Who said anything about fighting?” he mumbled in response, kissing the space beneath Mydei’s jaw, fingers pressing into his side as he moved above him.

Mydei looped an arm around his shoulder, leaning up to kiss him. “We’re never finishing that crib at this rate.”

☼ 

The sheets were cool when Mydei reached out, his hand patting the empty space where Phainon should’ve been. He stirred, brows furrowing in sleep before he finally opened his eyes. 

He stayed still for a moment, listening. 

He could hear the faint clatter of keys from the living room. 

Mydei sighed, pushing the blanket aside and sitting up slowly. He could've gone back to sleep, but the emptiness in his chest wouldn't settle. The shift happened a few weeks ago. He'd wanted to be close to Phainon every waking second. He'd curl up next to him on the couch while he was studying, cuddle with him in bed before he fell asleep, and just a few days ago he'd found himself following him to the kitchen when he was getting a glass of water. 

Mydei blamed the baby. It was definitely her doing. 

He padded into the hallway, yawning. The living room was dimly lit by the lamp on the side table, casting warm light over Phainon’s face amidst his mess of open books on the coffee table. 

Phainon looked up when he heard the creak of the floorboard. “Sorry—didn’t mean to wake you.”

“You didn’t,” Mydei said, crossing the room. “What are you doing up?”

Phainon reached out instinctively, tugging Mydei to sit in his lap. “I have an exam,” he murmured, pressing his lips against his shoulder. “I wanted to get through the readings while it was quiet.”

“You’ll be too tired for the exam if you keep this up.” Mydei narrowed his eyes at the mess around them. “Come to bed. Just for a bit.”

Phainon hesitated. 

“Phainon, my love,” Mydei said softly, knowing that would do the trick. He knew Phainon had weaknesses, and Mydei, well, he was one of them. “Please come to bed," he batted his eyelashes for a little extra flare. 

That was all it took. Phainon let out a breath and closed his laptop. 

“Alright,” he said, helping Mydei up. “You win.”

“I always do,” Mydei teased as they headed back to the bedroom together as Phainon muttered something about setting an early alarm and telling Mydei to make sure he wakes up. 

☼

It was quiet. 

Mydei sat on the edge of the bed, one hand braced on the mattress, the other pressed to his abdomen as the tight, rhythmic ache settled in. He breathed in through his nose, out through his mouth. He’d already timed the contractions. They were close together now. 

It was time. 

And Phainon was still in the middle of his exam. 

He’d left earlier in the morning after Mydei had assured him that nothing would happen in the three hours he was gone. Mydei had kissed him three times and told him to go before he failed just because he didn’t show up on time. 

“I’ll be here when you’re done.” he's said. 

That had clearly been a lie. 

A sharp wave of pressure rolled through him again, and Mydei had to pause, clutching the side of the bed, breathing hard. His eyes watered slightly, but it wasn’t out of fear. Not entirely at least. It was everything. The pain, the timing, the fact that the father of his child was across town with no way to contact him. 

He grabbed his phone from the nightstand with trembling fingers. 

It’s time

Don’t panic. Just come when you’re done. I’m okay

He paused, the added: 

I love you

He pressed send and stood slowly, grabbing the hospital bag by the door with one hand, the other resting against his stomach. 

“You couldn’t have waited two more hours?” he muttered to her with a wince as the knock sounded at the door.

He’d barely made it to the hallway when another sharp wave hit him, stealing the breath from his lungs. He braced himself against the wall, eyes squeezing shut. 

He opened the door to reveal Cipher and Castorice on the other end. 

“Wooow you’re pale,” Cipher said immediately, twirling her keys on her finger. "This is sooo not your look."

“He’s in labour, Cipher. This is not the time,” Castorice said, already moving to grab the hospital bag from him, and steadying him.  “Is Phainon still taking that exam?”

Mydei nodded, not trusting his voice. 

“God, he has the worst timing,” Cipher sighed, grabbing Mydei’s other arm. "First he leaves after planting one in you and now he isn't even here to see it through."

"He'll—" Another contraction surged and Mydei gritted his teeth, "be there," he said, mostly reassuring himself as he grabbed Castorice’s arm. Her grip steadied him, her voice low and soothing. 

“Deep breaths, De. Good. Again.”

When it passed, Mydei let out a long exhale. “Okay. We need to go now.”

☼

The delivery room was buzzing, monitors softly beeping to the rhythm of Mydei’s heartbeat. The nurse next to him was calm and gentle as she coaxed him to breathe through the next wave. 

He gritted his teeth, sweat on his brow, both hands gripping the side rails. He knew it was time. Everything in his body told him it was time, but he shook his head. 

“Not yet,” he gasped. “Not yet. He’s not here.”

The nurse glanced toward the clock. “I know you’re waiting for your partner, but—”

"No, I can't—he has to be here."

“Mydei!” 

Phainon’s voice cut through the chaos and Mydei’s head turned, eyes wide, then instantly filled with tears. 

Phainon was already at his side, dropping his bad to the floor, cupping Mydei’s face with shaking hands. 

“I’m here. I’m here,” he whispered. “I got here as fast as I could. I thought I’d miss it. I’m sorry—I’m so sorry.”

Mydei shook his head. “It’s not your fau—” he groaned when another wave of pain hit him. 

The nurse’s voice broke gently into the moment. “Alright, Mydei. I need you to push, okay?”

Phainon brushed the hair away from Mydei’s forehead. Mydei glanced up at him, reaching for his hand, squeezing it as Phainon whispered gentle reassurances to him.  

It was time to meet her.
